subject: MAP: Evaluation acceptance probes, exit gates & decision guardrails
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@medilytics.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@medilytics.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-19T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Evaluation acceptance probes & acceptance checklist

Hi Nikhil —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. Medilytics is excited about Redwood’s performance and the routing/cost controls you showed. Before we move procurement, Legal and our Cloud Ops want a tightly scoped Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that makes the evaluation objective and auditable. Specifically we need:

- A short catalog of acceptance probes (concrete tests) with pass/fail thresholds (latency p95, token-per-request quotas, top-N accuracy checks for reranking).
- Clear exit gates (what constitutes a pass to move to trial and what triggers an extended evaluation or rollback).
- A proposed 6-week close timeline aligned to procurement cutover dates.

Can you share a MAP draft that includes the acceptance tests (preferably a table) and any attachments we can pass to Procurement and Security? We have a target to complete procurement review by 2026-09-30.

Also: our security team will submit a SOC/technical questionnaire next week — if you can call out which probes require additional evidence (logs, audit trails, KMS integration docs), that will help speed review.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Head of Platform Engineering — Medilytics
Alicia.Ramos@medilytics.com

Attachments: procurement_requirements.pdf (stub)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@medilytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Evaluation acceptance probes & acceptance checklist

Alicia —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass MAP (MAP_v1.3.xlsx) and a companion markdown "eval_probe_catalog.md" that enumerates each probe and the objective measurement we propose. High level summary below — full details in the attachments.

Key acceptance probes (summary):
- Latency: p95 < 220ms for single-stream text generation at target load (10 rps sustained) — measured at customer ingress point.
- Throughput: end-to-end sustained throughput >= 6k tokens/min per reserved GPU pool during batch runs.
- Functional: reranker top-5 recall >= 92% on Medilytics validation set (slice: clinical notes).
- Safety/Concordance: hallucination rate < 2% on named-entity extraction checks (scripted eval).
- Observability: token-level billing match within 1% vs customer telemetry for 48h sample.

Exit gates (pass / soft-fail / fail):
- Pass -> All probes green and security checklist complete for SOC evidence items listed. Move to pilot (reserved capacity) and procurement signs the SOW.
- Soft-fail -> One non-critical probe (e.g., throughput within 10%) triggers a 2-week remediation sprint and re-test.
- Fail -> More than one critical probe (latency or top-5 recall) fails -> extend evaluation or switch to fall-back model variant.

We call out which probes require attachments: observability (audit logs sample), KMS integration (KMS config snapshot), and safety (scripted eval outputs). See eval_probe_catalog.md for file names and sample commands.

Proposed timeline (deliverables & owners):
- Week 0 (8/24): Deliver MAP_v1.3 + probe scripts (Redwood) — DONE after this mail.
- Week 1 (8/30): Smoke-run with Medilytics engineering (joint) — baseline metrics collected.
- Week 2 (9/6): Full probe run (48h) and initial evaluation.
- Week 3 (9/13): Security review (SOC evidence handoff) and remediation if needed.
- Week 4 (9/20): Final verification run.
- Week 5 (9/27): Sign-off window and procurement SOW finalization.

Attachments: MAP_v1.3.xlsx (MAP table), eval_probe_catalog.md (probe list + scripts).

If Ben/Marissa have suggested additions, happy to iterate — we can also embed sample k6 scripts or trace collectors.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com

Attachment: MAP_v1.3.xlsx (stub), eval_probe_catalog.md (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Evaluation acceptance probes & acceptance checklist

Looping in a few operational items from our side — quick points we should add to the probe catalog before we send to Procurement: 

- Smoke test checklist (pre-run): env parity verification, model variant pin, tokenization sanity sample. Add as a 10-step checklist.
- Performance guardrails: set automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant if p95 > 350ms for >5 minutes (documented runbook).
- Rollback triggers (critical): repeated top-5 recall degradation > 4% across two probe runs or safety metric regression > 1% absolute -> automatic throttle + incident review.
- Evidence envelope: include single-click instructions for how Medilytics can pull audit logs for a 72h window (we'll attach the logs script into eval_probe_catalog.md).

Marissa — can you confirm the acceptance test owners (we usually propose Redwood for probe orchestration, Medilytics to run client-side ingestion tests, Security to validate evidence)? Also, I suggest adding an "acceptance sign-off matrix" to the spreadsheet so Legal/PM can tick off responsibilities.

Ben Carter
Platform Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

This looks good and actionable, thank you. A couple quick notes from our side:

- Security: I'll have our Security lead review the evidence envelope (audit logs script + KMS checklist). Expect feedback by 09/03.
- Timeline: Medilytics can commit to the smoke run week starting 2026-08-30 and the 48h full probe on 09/06 as proposed. If probes pass, Procurement will start the SOW approval and we aim for signature the week of 09/27.

Next steps: please circulate the updated MAP_v1.3 with Ben's rollback triggers and the added sign-off matrix. I'll confirm the Procurement contact and share the initial SOW template.

Thanks — looking forward to the joint run.
